<B><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">PART I</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><U><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Item 1.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Business</FONT></U></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Alliance Bancorp, Inc. of Pennsylvania (&#8220;Alliance Bancorp&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a Pennsylvania corporation and a savings and loan holding company which owns 100% of the capital stock of Alliance Bank (</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#8220;Bank&#8221;), which is a Pennsylvania chartered community oriented savings bank headquartered in Broomall, Pennsylvania.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On January 18, 2011, Alliance Mutual Holding Company and Alliance Bancorp, Inc. of Pennsylvania, the federally chartered former mid-tier holding company for the Bank (the &#8220;Mid-Tier Holding Company&#8221;) completed a reorganization and conversion (the &#8220;second step conversion&#8221;), pursuant to which the Company (a new Pennsylvania corporation) acquired all the issued and outstanding shares of the Bank&#8217;s common stock.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In connection with the second step conversion, 3,258,475 shares of common stock, par value $0.01 per share, of the Company<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>were sold in subscription, community and syndicated community offerings to certain depositors of the Bank and other investors for $10 per share, or $32.6 million in the aggregate (the &#8220;Offering), and 2,215,962 shares of common stock were issued in exchange for the outstanding shares of common stock of the Mid-Tier Holding Company held by the &#8220;public&#8221; shareholders of the Mid-Tier Holding Company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Each share of common stock of the Mid-Tier Holding Company was converted into the right to receive 0.8200 shares of common stock of the Company in the second step conversion.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a result of the second step conversion, the former mutual holding company and the Mid-Tier Company were merged into Alliance Bancorp and 548,524 (pre-conversion) treasury shares were canceled.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Additionally, the Bank&#8217;s Employee Stock Ownership Plan (&#8220;ESOP&#8221;) was issued a line of credit for up to $1.9 million, which it used to purchase 50,991 shares of common stock in the Offering and 100,000 additional shares of common stock in the open market following the Offering.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Alliance Bancorp is the successor to the Mid-Tier Holding Company and references to Alliance Bancorp or the Company include reference to the former Mid-Tier Holding Company where applicable. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Alliance Bank operates a total of eight banking offices located in Delaware and Chester Counties, Pennsylvania, which are suburbs of Philadelphia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our primary business consists of attracting deposits from the general public and using those funds, together with funds we borrow, to originate loans to our customers and invest in securities such as U.S. Government and agency securities, mortgage-backed securities and municipal obligations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company had $425.5 million of total assets, $345.4 million of total deposits and stockholders&#8217; equity of $70.2 million.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is subject to supervision and regulation by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve Board System (the &#8220;FRB&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank is subject to regulation by the Pennsylvania Department of Banking and Securities (the "Department"), as its chartering authority and primary regulator, and by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC"), which insures the Bank's deposits up to applicable limits.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Market Area and Competition</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Alliance Bank is headquartered in Broomall, Pennsylvania and conducts its business through eight branches located in Delaware County, Pennsylvania, and one office in Chester County, Pennsylvania.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The primary market areas served by Alliance Bank are Delaware and Chester Counties, Philadelphia, and the suburban areas to the west and south of Philadelphia, including southern New Jersey.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Delaware and Chester Counties have a large, well-educated, and skilled labor force, with nearly one quarter of the counties&#8217; population having earned a four-year college degree. In addition, Philadelphia&#8217;s central location in the Northeast corridor, infrastructure, and other factors have made the Bank&#8217;s primary market area attractive to many large corporate employers, including Comcast, Boeing, State Farm Insurance, Main Line Health Systems, Janseen Pharmaceuticals, United Parcel Service, PECO Energy, SAP America, Inc. and Wawa. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Philadelphia area economy is typical of many large northeastern cities where the traditional manufacturing-based economy has declined and been replaced by the service sector, including the health care market. Crozer/Keystone Health System, Main Line Health, Jefferson Health System, Mercy Health Corp., and Astra-Zeneca are among the larger health care employers within the Bank&#8217;s market area. According to the Delaware County Chamber of Commerce, there are more than 65 degree-granting institutions in the Delaware Valley region, representing a higher density of colleges and universities than any other area in the United States. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD

</TD>
  <TD

  <DIV

</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The population of Delaware County is reported at over half a million residents and is the fifth most populated county in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. Much of the growth and development continues to be in the western part of the county and in adjacent Chester County. Chester County&#8217;s growth rate is expected to increase even further in the next decade, and some of the communities in Chester County that are experiencing the most rapid growth &#151; East Whiteland Township, New Garden Township and East Goshen &#151; surround the Bank&#8217;s Chester County branch. We face strong competition, both in attracting deposits and making real estate and commercial loans. Our most direct competition for deposits has historically come from other savings banks, credit unions, and commercial banks located in our market area. This includes many large regional financial institutions and internet banks which have even greater financial and marketing resources available to them. The ability of the Bank to attract and retain core deposits depends on its ability to provide a competitive rate of return, liquidity, and service convenience comparable to those offered by competing investment opportunities. The Bank&#8217;s management remains focused on attracting core deposits through its branch network, business development efforts, and commercial business relationships.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Lending Activities</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General.</FONT></B><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company's total portfolio of loans receivable amounted to $303.9 million, or 71.4%, of the Company's $425.5 million of total assets at such time.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Over the past 15 years, the Company has placed an emphasis on loans secured by commercial real estate properties.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Consistent with such approach, commercial real estate loans amounted to $122.8 million or 40.4% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2013 while single family residential mortgage loans amounted to $124.2 million or 40.9% of the total loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>To a lesser extent, the Company also originates multi-family loans, land and construction loans, consumer loans and commercial business loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, such loan categories amounted to $22.2 million, $19.8 million, $4.5 million and $10.4 million, respectively, or 7.3%, 6.5%, 1.5% and 3.4% of the total loan portfolio, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company intends to continue the origination of single-family residential mortgage loans as well as the origination of commercial real estate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For the year ended December 31, 2013, the Company&#8217;s single-family mortgage loans decreased by $2.5 million or 1.9% to $124.2 million.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>For the year ended December 31, 2013, the Company&#8217;s commercial real estate loans increased by $11.5 million or 10.3% to $122.8 million. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Scheduled contractual amortization of loans does not reflect the expected term of the Company's loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The average life of loans is substantially less than their contractual terms because of prepayments and due-on-sale clauses, which gives the Company the right to declare a conventional loan immediately due and payable in the event, among other things, that the borrower sells the real property subject to the mortgage and the loan is not repaid.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The average life of mortgage loans tends to increase when current mortgage loan rates are higher than rates on existing mortgage loans and, conversely, decrease when rates on existing mortgage loans are lower than current mortgage loan rates (due to refinancings of adjustable-rate and fixed-rate loans at lower rates).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the latter circumstance, the weighted average yield on the loan portfolio decreases as higher-yielding loans are repaid or refinanced at lower rates.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s single-family loan originations amounted to $12.7 million and $13.9 million during 2013 and 2012, respectively. When possible, we emphasize the origination of single-family residential adjustable-rate mortgage loans (&#8220;ARMs&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Originations of such loans amounted to $125,000 and $1.3 million during 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We also originate fixed-rate single-family residential real estate loans with terms of five, ten, 15, 20, 25 and 30 years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally, as part of our asset/liability strategies, fixed rate residential mortgage loans with terms greater than 15 years have been originated pursuant to commitments to sell such loans to correspondent mortgage-banking institutions in order to reduce the proportion of the loan portfolio comprised of such assets and reduce our interest rate risk.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans are sold without any recourse to the Company by the purchaser in the event of default on the loan by the borrower and are generally sold with servicing released.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We had no sales of residential mortgage loans for the years ended December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 2px solid; FONT-STYLE: normal; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In accordance with the Company&#8217;s increased emphasis on commercial real estate loan originations in recent years, such originations amounted to $34.5 million and $28.0 million during 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, land and construction loan originations amounted to $35.1 million and $23.5 million during 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Since 1999, the Company has originated some single-family residential loan products to borrowers that did not meet the underwriting criteria of the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (&#8216;FHLMC&#8221;) and the Federal National Mortgage Association (&#8220;FNMA&#8221;) and where the borrower&#8217;s credit score is below 660.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company recognizes that these loans, which are considered subprime loans, have additional risk factors as compared to typical single-family residential lending.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans are generally not saleable in the secondary market due to the credit risk characteristics of the borrower, the underlying documentation, the loan-to-value ratio, or the size of the loan, among other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013 and 2012, the Company&#8217;s single-family loan portfolio included $15.5 million or 12.4% and $17.0 million or 13.4%, respectively, of such subprime loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>The Company reported $433,000 or 2.8% and $1.4 million or 8.2% of these loans as nonperforming at December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company recognizes the additional risk factors associated with subprime lending and utilizes a higher risk-weighting factor in maintaining its allowance for loan losses with respect to these loans. In addition, management calculates and reports the delinquency ratio of its subprime loan portfolio to the Board of Directors on a monthly basis.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times-Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Historically, we have not been an active purchaser of loans. However, we purchased $893,000 of loans during the year ended December 31, 2013 and $128,000 during the year ended December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Substantially all of our purchased loans were secured by properties located in Pennsylvania. As of December 31, 2013, the outstanding balance of our purchased loans amounted to $2.2 million and included $333,000 of multifamily real estate loans, $191,000 of single-family residential real estate loans, and $1.7 million of commercial real estate loans. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times-Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a Pennsylvania-chartered savings bank, Alliance Bank is not subject to any specific regulatory limits on the size of the loans that it may originate. However, we generally have adhered to an &#8220;in-house&#8221; policy limit that loans outstanding to any one borrower including such borrower&#8217;s affiliates will not exceed 15% of the Bank&#8217;s capital.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Single-Family Residential Real Estate Loans</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company originates residential loans secured primarily by first mortgage liens on existing single-family residences. The Company also originates shorter term home equity loans which may be secured by first or second mortgages.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, $124.2 million or 40.9% of the Company's total loan portfolio consisted of single-family residential real estate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Of the $124.2 million of such loans at December 31, 2013, $19.3 million or 15.5% had adjustable rates of interest and $104.9 million or 84.5% had fixed rates of interest.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s ARMs typically provide for an interest rate which adjusts every year after an initial period of three, five, seven or ten years in accordance with a designated index (the national monthly median cost of funds or the weekly average yield on U.S. Treasury securities adjusted to a constant comparable maturity of one year) plus a margin.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such loans are typically based on a 30-year amortization schedule.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amount of any increase or decrease in the interest rate is presently limited to 200 basis points per year, with a limit of 600 basis points over the life of the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>The Company has not engaged in the practice of using a cap on the payments that could allow the loan balance to increase rather than decrease, resulting in negative amortization.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The adjustable-rate loans offered by the Company, like many other financial institutions, provide for initial rates of interest below the rates which would prevail when the index used for repricing is applied.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, the Company underwrites loans on the basis of the borrower's ability to pay at the initial rate which would be in effect without the discount.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Although the Company continues to emphasize ARMs, such loan products have not been as attractive due to the lower interest rate environment which has prevailed since the recession, resulting in a greater demand for fixed rate loans.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Adjustable-rate loans decrease the risks to the Company that are associated with changes in interest rates but involve other risks, primarily because as interest rates rise, the payment by the borrower rises to the extent permitted by the terms of the loan, thereby increasing the potential for default.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>The Company believes that these risks, which have not had a material adverse effect on the Company to date, generally are less than the risks associated with holding fixed-rate loans in an increasing interest rate environment.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has continued to originate a limited amount of fixed-rate mortgage loans with terms up to 30 years. Generally, the Company emphasizes the origination of fixed-rate loans with terms of 15 years or less for its portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, while the Company offers balloon loans with five, seven, ten, and 15 year terms based on a 20 to 30 year amortization schedule, the Company has only originated a small amount of such loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Many of these types of loans may not qualify under the new regulatory guidelines known as &#8220;qualified residential mortgages&#8221; (QRM).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a result of these new rules the Company is reevaluating the risks associated with making loans that are &#8220;QRM&#8221; versus loans that are outside &#8220;QRM&#8221; guidelines which although are permissible result in other types of risks.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company also offers home equity loans with fixed rates of interest and terms of 15 years or less.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company does not require that it hold the first mortgage on the secured property; however, the balance on all mortgages on the secured property cannot exceed 90% of the value of the secured property.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company held a first lien on a majority of the properties securing home equity loans from the Company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, home equity loans and lines amounted to $12.5 million or 4.1% of the total loan portfolio, which are included in single family loans.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is permitted to lend up to 100% of the appraised value of the real property securing a residential loan; however, if the amount of a residential loan originated or refinanced exceeds 90% of the appraised value, the Company is required by federal regulations to obtain private mortgage insurance on the portion of the principal amount that exceeds 80% of the appraised value of the security property.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Pursuant to underwriting guidelines adopted by the Board of Directors, the Company may lend up to an 80% loan-to-value ratio without private mortgage insurance unless it is determined that additional collateral in the form of private mortgage insurance or other acceptable collateral is needed.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company may lend up to a 90% loan-to-value ratio on a one or two family owner-occupied residential property as long as additional collateral in the form of private mortgage insurance or other acceptable collateral enhancements are obtained. Exceptions to this policy may be made to assist in the Company's community outreach efforts if deemed prudent by the Company's management and with additional collateral enhancements to reduce the risk inherent in the loan(s).</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Multi-Family Residential and Commercial Real Estate Loans</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company originates and, to a lesser extent, purchases mortgage loans for the acquisition and refinancing of existing multi-family residential and commercial real estate properties.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, $22.2 million or 7.3% of the Company's total loan portfolio consisted of loans secured by existing multi-family residential real estate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, $122.8 million or 40.4% of the Company's total loan portfolio consisted of loans secured by commercial real estate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The majority of the Company's multi-family residential loans are secured primarily by multi-unit residential and apartment buildings, while the Company&#8217;s commercial real estate loans are primarily secured by office buildings, hotels, small retail establishments, restaurants and other facilities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These types of properties constitute the majority of the Company's commercial real estate loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The majority of the multi-family residential and commercial real estate loan portfolio at December 31, 2013 was secured by properties located in the Company&#8217;s primary market area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2013, the five largest multi-family residential and commercial real estate loan relationships had outstanding balances of $9.0 million, $8.0 million, $7.5 million, $6.6 million and $6.4 million, respectively, all of which were performing in accordance with their terms and were current at such date.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Multi-family residential and commercial real estate loans are made on terms up to 30 years, some of which include call or balloon provisions ranging from five to 15 years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company will originate and purchase these loans either with fixed interest rates or with interest rates which adjust in accordance with a designated index.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan to value ratios on the Company's multi-family residential and commercial real estate loans are typically limited to 80% of appraised value at the time the loan is granted.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As part of the criteria for underwriting multi-family residential and commercial real estate loans, the Company generally imposes a debt coverage ratio (the ratio of net cash from operations before payment of debt service to debt service) of not less than 1.20.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is also the Company's general policy to obtain corporate or personal guarantees, as applicable, on its multi-family residential and commercial real estate loans from the principals of the borrower.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Multi-family residential and commercial real estate lending entails significant additional risks as compared with single-family residential property lending.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such loans typically involve large loan balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The payment experience on such loans is typically dependent on the successful operation of the real estate project.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The success of such projects is sensitive to changes in supply and demand conditions in the market for multi-family and commercial real estate as well as economic conditions generally.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company had no nonperforming multi-family residential loans and three nonperforming commercial real estate loans with balances of $744,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company had no multi-family loans and nine commercial real estate loans in the amount of $4.5 million that were considered performing troubled debt restructurings.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Construction Loans.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company also originates residential and commercial construction loans, and to a limited degree, land acquisition and development loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Construction loans are classified as either residential construction loans or commercial real estate construction loans at the time of origination, depending on the nature of the property securing the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company's construction lending activities generally are limited to the Company's primary market area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, construction loans amounted to $19.8 million or 6.5% of the Company's total loan portfolio, which consisted of $4.0 million of residential and $15.8 million of commercial real estate construction loans.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 2px solid; FONT-STYLE: normal; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company's residential construction loans are primarily made to local real estate builders and developers for the purpose of constructing single-family homes and single-family residential developments.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Upon successful application, credit review and analysis of personal and corporate financial statements, the Company will grant local builders construction loans, construction to permanent loans, and/or lines of credit up to designated amounts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans may be used for the purpose of constructing model homes, including a limited number for inventory.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In some instances, lines of credit will also be granted for purposes of acquiring improved lots or the purchase of construction in process and developing of speculative properties thereon.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Once approved for a construction loan or credit line, a developer submits a progress report and a request for payment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally, the Company makes payments under the stage of completion method.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Prior to making payment, the Company inspects all construction sites and verifies that the work being submitted for payments has been performed.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s commercial construction loans are generally made to local developers and others for the purpose of developing commercial real estate properties such as small office buildings and hotels, storage facilities and commercial building renovations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The application, credit review and disbursement process are similar to those mentioned above for the Company&#8217;s residential construction loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2013 the five largest real estate construction loans had outstanding balances of $4.5 million, $1.9 million, $1.8 million, $1.3 million, and $1.0 million, respectively, all of which were performing in accordance with their terms and were current at such date.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company's construction loans generally have maturities of 12 to 36 months, with payments being made monthly on an interest-only basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These interest payments are generally paid out of an interest reserve, which is established in connection with the origination of the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally, such loans adjust monthly based on the prime rate plus a margin of up to 2.0%. Residential and commercial real estate construction loans are generally made with maximum loan to value ratios of 80% and 75%, respectively, on an as completed basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>The Company utilizes interest rate floors on commercial loans and lines of credit whenever possible.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Construction lending is generally considered to involve a higher level of risk as compared to single-family residential lending, due to the concentration of principal in a limited number of loans and borrowers and the effects of general economic conditions on developers and builders.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Moreover, a construction loan can involve additional risks because of the inherent difficulty in estimating both a property's value at completion of the project and the estimated cost (including interest) of the project.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The nature of these loans is such that they are generally more difficult to evaluate and monitor. In addition, construction loans may include speculative construction loans to a builder where the homes are not necessarily pre-sold and thus pose a greater potential risk to the Company than construction loans to individuals on their personal residences.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has attempted to minimize the foregoing risks by, among other things, limiting the number of units built to one or two sample units plus any units under agreement of sale and limiting the extent of its construction lending. The Company&#8217;s underwriting guidelines impose stringent loan-to-value, debt service, borrower liquidity, and other requirements for loans which are believed to involve higher elements of credit risk, by limiting the geographic area in which the Company will do business and by working with builders with whom it has established relationships.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company had no nonperforming construction loans.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Consumer Loans</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company offers consumer loans in order to provide a full range of financial services to its customers and because such loans generally have shorter terms and higher interest rates than mortgage loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The consumer loans presently offered by the Company include deposit account secured loans and lines of credit.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company withdrew from providing student loans in 2010.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Consumer loans amounted to $4.5 million or 1.5% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Student loans amounted to $4.2 million or 1.4% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such loans were made to local students for a term of ten years, presently with adjustable interest rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The interest rate is determined by the U.S. Department of Education.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan repayment obligations do not begin until the student has completed his or her education.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The principal and interest on such loans is guaranteed by the U.S. Government.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans secured by deposit accounts amounted to $223,000 or 0.1% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such loans are originated for up to 90% of the account balance, with a hold placed on the account restricting the withdrawal of the account balance.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Consumer loans generally have shorter terms and higher interest rates than mortgage loans but generally involve more credit risk than mortgage loans because of the type and nature of the collateral and, in certain cases, the absence of collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, consumer lending collections are dependent on the borrower's continuing financial stability, and thus are more likely to be adversely effected by job loss, divorce, illness and personal bankruptcy.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In most cases, any repossessed collateral for a defaulted consumer loan will not provide an adequate source of repayment of the outstanding loan balance because of improper repair and maintenance of the underlying collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The remaining deficiency often does not warrant further substantial collection efforts against the borrower.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company believes that the generally higher yields earned on consumer loans compensate for the increased credit risk associated with such loans and that consumer loans are important to its efforts to provide a full range of services to its customers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, there were 113 nonperforming student loans which amounted to $412,000, compared to 93 nonperforming student loans which amounted to $324,000 at December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All of these nonperforming student loans are fully guaranteed by the U.S. Government.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Commercial Business Loans.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company has a commercial loan department, which provides a full range of commercial loan products to small business customers in its primary marketing area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans generally have shorter terms and higher interest rates as compared to mortgage loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such loans amounted to $10.4 million or 3.4% of the total loan portfolio at December 31, 2013 and were primarily secured by inventories and other business assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although commercial business loans generally are considered to involve greater credit risk than other certain types of loans, management intends to continue to offer commercial business loans to small businesses located in its primary market area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, the Company had no nonperforming commercial business loans.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loan Fee Income</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition to interest earned on loans, the Company receives income from fees in connection with loan originations, loan modifications, late payments, prepayments and for miscellaneous services related to its loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Income from these activities varies from period to period with the volume and type of loans made and competitive conditions. The Company charges loan origination fees which are calculated as a percentage of the amount borrowed.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan origination and commitment fees and all incremental direct loan origination costs are deferred and recognized over the contractual remaining lives of the related loans on a level yield basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Discounts and premiums on loans purchased are amortized in the same manner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Asset Quality</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans are placed on non-accrual status when, in the judgment of management, the probability of collection of principal and interest is deemed to be insufficient to warrant further accrual.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Generally, when a loan is placed on nonaccrual status, unpaid interest credited to income in the current year is reversed and unpaid interest accrued in prior years is charged against the allowance for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company does not accrue interest on real estate loans past due 90 days or more unless, in the opinion of management, the value of the property securing the loan exceeds the outstanding balance of the loan (principal, interest and escrows) and collection is in process.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company provides an allowance for accrued interest deemed uncollectible.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such allowance amounted to approximately $240,000 at December 31, 2013 compared to $373,000 at December 31, 2012. Accrued interest receivable is reported net of the allowance for uncollected interest.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans may be reinstated to accrual status when all payments are brought current and, in the opinion of management, collection of the remaining balance of principal and interest can be reasonably expected.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Real estate acquired by the Company as a result of foreclosure or by deed-in-lieu of foreclosure is classified as other real estate owned (&#8220;OREO&#8221;) until sold and is initially recorded at the fair value less cost to sell at the date of acquisition establishing a new cost basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>After the date of acquisition, all costs incurred in maintaining the property are expensed and costs incurred for the improvement or development of such property are capitalized up to the extent of their fair value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2013, the Company had $3.2 million in OREO.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The $3.2 million of OREO consists of three commercial real estate properties in the amount of $1.4 million, three improved single family building lots totaling $870,000, and seven single family properties totaling $889,000, substantially all of which are located within the Company&#8217;s primary market area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("GAAP"), the Company is required to account for certain loan modifications or restructurings as "troubled debt restructurings."<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In general, the modification or restructuring of a debt constitutes a troubled debt restructuring if the Company, for economic or legal reasons related to the borrower's financial difficulties, grants a concession to the borrower that the Company would not otherwise consider.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Debt restructurings or loan modifications for a borrower do not necessarily always constitute troubled debt restructurings, however, and troubled debt restructurings do not necessarily result in non-accrual loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company had eleven loans classified as performing troubled debt restructurings consisting of two single-family loans which amounted to $361,000 and nine commercial real estate loans which amounted to $4.5 million.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All such loans have been performing in accordance with their restructured terms and conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company had one single family real estate nonperforming loan classified as a troubled debt restructuring in the amount of $191,000.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Nonperforming assets decreased $2.0 million to $5.7 million or 1.35% of total assets at December 31, 2013 as compared to $7.7 million or 1.67% of total assets at December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The nonperforming assets at December 31, 2013 included $2.5 million in nonperforming loans and $3.2 million in OREO.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The decrease in nonperforming assets was primarily due to a $2.0 million decrease in nonperforming loans, partially offset by a $1.1 million increase in other real estate owned as of December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Overall, nonperforming loans included $1.4 million in single-family residential real estate loans, $744,000 in commercial real estate loans, and $412,000 in student loans, which are fully guaranteed by the U.S. Government.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company continues to aggressively work towards the resolution of its nonperforming assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The allowance for loan losses amounted to $4.2 million or 166.7% of nonperforming loans at December 31, 2013 as compared to $4.9 million or 87.8% at December 31, 2012.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Classified and Criticized Assets.</FONT></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under applicable banking regulations and policies, each</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times-Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> insured savings bank&#8217;s assets are subject to classification on a regular basis. In addition, in connection with examinations of insured institutions, federal examiners have authority to identify problem assets and, if appropriate, classify them. There are three regulatory classifications for problem assets: &#8220;substandard,&#8221; &#8220;doubtful&#8221; and &#8220;loss.&#8221; Substandard assets have one or more defined weaknesses and are characterized by the distinct possibility that the insured institution will sustain some loss if the deficiencies are not corrected. Doubtful assets have the weaknesses of substandard assets with the additional characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions and values questionable, and there is a high possibility of loss. An asset classified loss is considered uncollectible and of such little value that continuance as an asset of the institution is not warranted. Another category designated &#8220;special mention&#8221; also must be established and maintained for assets which have a weakness but do not currently expose an insured institution to a sufficient degree of risk to warrant classification as substandard, doubtful or loss.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, the Company had $10.6 million of classified and criticized loans, of which $1.8 million consisted of loans designated as special mention, $8.8 million classified substandard loans and no assets classified as doubtful or loss.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The $1.8 million of loans designated as special mention consisted of $361,000 in single family real estate loans and $1.5 million in commercial real estate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The $8.8 million of loans designated as substandard consisted of $1.4 million in single family real estate loans and $7.4 million in commercial real estate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Substantially all of these loans are located in the Company&#8217;s primary market area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the Company had $3.2 million in OREO properties classified as substandard, substantially all of which are located in the Company&#8217;s primary market area.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Allowance for Loan Losses</FONT></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance for loan losses is increased by charges to income and decreased by chargeoffs (net of recoveries).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Allowances are provided for specific loans when losses are probable and can be estimated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>When this occurs, management considers the remaining principal balance, fair value and estimated net realizable value of the property collateralizing the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Current and future operating and/or sales conditions are also considered.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These estimates are susceptible to changes that could result in material adjustments to results of operations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Recovery of the carrying value of such loans is dependent to a great extent on economic, operating and other conditions that may be beyond management&#8217;s control.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General loan loss reserves are established as an allowance for losses based on inherent probable risk of loss in the loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In assessing risk, management considers historical experience, volume and composition of lending conducted by the Company, industry standards, status of nonperforming loans, general economic conditions as they relate to the market area and other factors related to the collectibility of the Company&#8217;s loan portfolio.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Impaired loans are predominantly measured based on the fair value of the collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The provision for loan losses charged to expense is based upon past loan loss experience and an evaluation of probable losses and impairment existing in the current loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A loan is considered to be impaired when, based upon current information and events, it is probable that the Company will be unable to collect all amounts due according to the original contractual terms of the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An insignificant delay or insignificant shortfall in amounts of payments does not necessarily result in the loan being identified as impaired.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For this purpose, delays less than 90 days are considered to be insignificant.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Large groups of smaller balance homogeneous loans, including residential real estate and consumer loans, are collectively evaluated for impairment, except for loans restructured under a troubled debt restructuring.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although management uses the best information available to make determinations with respect to the provisions for loan losses, additional provisions for loan losses may be required to be established in the future should economic or other conditions change substantially.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the Department and the FDIC, as an integral part of their examination process, periodically review the Company&#8217;s allowance for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such agencies may require the Company to recognize additions to such allowance based on their judgments about information available to them at the time of their examination.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Investment Activities</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Mortgage-Backed Securities.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Mortgage-backed securities (which also are known as mortgage participation certificates or pass-through certificates) represent a participation interest in a pool of single-family or multi-family mortgages, the principal and interest payments on which are passed from the mortgage originators, through intermediaries (generally U.S. Government agencies and government sponsored enterprises) that pool and repackage the participation interests in the form of securities, to investors such as the Company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such U.S. Government agencies and government sponsored enterprises, which guarantee the payment of principal and interest to investors, primarily include the FHLMC, the FNMA and the Government National Mortgage Association ("GNMA").</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times-Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The FHLMC is a public corporation chartered by the U.S. Government. The FHLMC issues participation certificates backed principally by conventional mortgage loans. The FHLMC guarantees the timely payment of interest and the ultimate return of principal within one year. The FNMA is a private corporation chartered by the U.S. Congress with a mandate to establish a secondary market for conventional mortgage loans. Because the FHLMC, the FNMA and the GNMA were established to provide support for low- and middle-income housing, there are limits to the maximum size of loans that qualify for these programs. To accommodate larger-sized loans, and loans that, for other reasons, do not conform to the agency programs, a number of private institutions have established their own home-loan origination and securitization programs.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times-Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Mortgage-backed securities typically are issued with stated principal amounts, and the securities are backed by pools of mortgages that have loans with interest rates that are within a range and have varying maturities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The cash flow associated with the underlying pool of mortgages, i.e., fixed rate or adjustable rate, as well as prepayment risk, are passed on to the certificate holder.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The life of a mortgage-backed pass-through security thus approximates the life of the underlying mortgages.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following table sets forth the fair value of the Company's mortgage-backed securities portfolio designated as available for sale at the dates indicated.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">_____________________</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(1) All mortgage-backed securities are designated as available for sale.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The actual maturity of a mortgage-backed security is typically less than its stated maturity due to prepayments of the underlying mortgages.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Prepayments that are faster than anticipated may shorten the life of the security and increase or decrease its yield to maturity if the security was purchased at a discount or premium, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The yield is based upon the interest income and the amortization of any premium or discount related to the mortgage-backed security.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In accordance with GAAP, premiums and discounts are amortized over the estimated lives of the loans, which decrease and increase interest income, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The prepayment assumptions used to determine the amortization period for premiums and discounts can significantly affect the yield of the mortgage-backed security, when premiums or discounts are involved, and these assumptions are reviewed periodically to reflect actual prepayments.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Although prepayments of underlying mortgages depend on many factors, including the type of mortgages, the coupon rate, the age of mortgages, the geographical location of the underlying real estate collateralizing the mortgages and general levels of market interest rates, the difference between the interest rates on the underlying mortgages and the prevailing mortgage interest rates generally is the most significant determinant of the rate of prepayments.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>During periods of falling mortgage interest rates, if the coupon rate of the underlying mortgages exceeds the prevailing market interest rates offered for mortgage loans, refinancing generally increases and accelerates the prepayment of the underlying mortgages and the related security.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under such circumstances, the Company may be subject to reinvestment risk because to the extent that the Company's mortgage-backed securities amortize or prepay faster than anticipated, the Company may not be able to reinvest the proceeds of such repayments and prepayments at a comparable rate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>During periods of rising interest rates, prepayment of the underlying mortgages generally slow down when the coupon rate of such mortgages is less than the prevailing market rate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company may be subject to extension risk when this occurs.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Investment Securities.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The investment policy of the Company, as established by the Board of Directors, is designed primarily to provide and maintain liquidity and to maximize return on investments without incurring undue interest rate risk, credit risk, and investment portfolio asset concentrations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company's investment policy takes into account the Company's business plan, interest rate management, the current economic environment, the types of securities to be held and other safety and soundness considerations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company's investment policy is currently implemented by the Chief Executive Officer and reviewed and evaluated by the Asset Liability Committee of the Board of Directors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Asset Liability Committee is required to issue a written compliance report to the Board of Directors at least quarterly.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(2) The $28.4 million of municipal obligations are designated as held to maturity and are tax exempt.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FHLB stock is a restricted investment security, carried at cost.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The purchase of FHLB stock provides banks with the right to be a member of the FHLB and to receive the products and services that the FHLB provides to member banking institutions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Unlike other types of stock, FHLB stock is acquired primarily for the right to receive advances from the FHLB, rather than the for the purpose of earning dividends or price appreciation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sources of Funds</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Deposits are the primary source of the Company's funds for lending and other investment purposes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition to deposits, the Company derives funds from loan principal repayments, prepayments and advances from the Federal Home Loan Bank (&#8220;FHLB&#8221;) of Pittsburgh and proceeds from sales of investment securities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan repayments are a relatively stable source of funds, while deposit inflows and outflows are significantly influenced by general interest rates and money market conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Borrowings may be used on a short-term basis to compensate for reductions in the availability of funds from other sources or to balance cash flows during times of high loan production.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>They may also be used on a longer term basis for general business purposes.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deposits</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company's deposit products include a broad selection of deposit instruments, including NOW accounts, money market accounts, regular savings accounts and term certificate accounts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Deposit account terms vary, with the principal difference being the minimum balance required, the time periods the funds must remain on deposit and the interest rate.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The primary market areas served by the Company are Delaware and Chester Counties, Philadelphia, and the suburban areas to the west and south of Philadelphia, including southern New Jersey.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;</FONT>The Company attracts deposit accounts by offering a wide variety of accounts, competitive interest rates, and convenient office locations and service hours.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the Company maintains automated teller machines at its Broomall, Concordville, Havertown, Springfield, Lansdowne, Frazer, and Secane offices.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company utilizes traditional marketing methods to attract new customers and savings deposits, including print media advertising and direct mailings.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company does not advertise for deposits outside of its primary market area or utilize the services of deposit brokers, and management believes that an insignificant number of deposit accounts were held by non-residents of Pennsylvania at December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has been competitive in the types of accounts and in interest rates it has offered on its deposit products but does not necessarily seek to match the highest rates paid by competing institutions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Although market demand generally dictates which deposit maturities and rates will be accepted by the public, the Company intends to continue to promote longer term deposits to the extent possible and consistent with its asset and liability management goals.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 95%; FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company had 80 full-time employees and 18 part-time employees at December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>None of these employees is represented by a collective bargaining agreement.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
