  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Recent Accounting Pronouncements &#150; </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July 2013, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) No. 2013-11, <I>&#8220;Presentation of an Unrecognized Tax Benefit When a Net Operating Loss Carryforward, a Similar Tax Loss, or a Tax Credit Carryforward Exists.&#8221;&#160;</I> &#160;This amendment addresses the financial statement presentation of an unrecognized tax benefit, or a portion of an unrecognized tax benefit, as a reduction to a deferred tax asset for a net operating loss carryforward, a similar tax loss, or a tax credit carryforward. The amendments in this Update are effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December 15, 2013. Early adoption is permitted. The amendments should be applied prospectively to all unrecognized tax benefits that exist at the effective date.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this ASU is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In February&#160;2013, the FASB issued ASU 2013-02, &#8220; <I>Comprehensive Income, Reporting of Amounts Reclassified Out of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (Topic 220).</I> &#8221; The amendments in this update aim to improve the reporting of reclassifications out of accumulated other comprehensive income.&#160; The amendments in this update seek to attain that objective by requiring an entity to report the effect of significant reclassifications out of accumulated other comprehensive income on the respective line items in net income if the amount being reclassified is required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified in its entirety to net income.&#160; For other amounts that are not required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified in their entirety to net income in the same reporting period, an entity is required to cross-reference other disclosures required under U.S. GAAP that provide additional detail about those amounts. This would be the case when a portion of the amount reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income is reclassified to a balance sheet account instead of directly to income or expense in the same reporting period.&#160; For public entities, the amendments are effective prospectively for reporting periods beginning after December&#160;15, 2012. The adoption of this Update did not have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and the Company has included the required disclosures from ASU 2013-02 in the consolidated financial statements.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013, management believes that the estimated fair values of the securities disclosed above are primarily dependent upon the movement in market interest rates particularly given the negligible inherent credit risk associated with these securities. These investment securities are comprised of securities that are rated investment grade by at least one bond credit rating service. Although the fair value will fluctuate as the market interest rates move, management believes that these fair values will recover as the underlying portfolios mature. As of December 31, 2013, there were 14 U.S. government obligations, no mortgage-backed securities, and 15 municipal securities in an unrealized loss position.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Of the securities in an unrealized loss position at December 31, 2013, there was one municipal security in an unrealized loss position for twelve months or longer.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>The Company does not intend to sell and it is not more likely than not that the Company will be required to sell these securities until such time as the value recovers or the securities mature. Management does not believe any individual unrealized loss as of December 31, 2013 represents an other-than-temporary impairment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, the Company had eleven loans classified as performing troubled debt restructurings consisting of two single-family loans which amounted to $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">361,000</FONT> and nine commercial real estate loans which amounted to $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">4.5</FONT> million.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The two single-family loans were classified as special mention in the Company&#8217;s allowance for loan losses and have no allowance against them.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Five of the nine commercial real estate loans, which amounted to $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.5</FONT> million are classified as special mention in the Company&#8217;s allowance for loan losses and have a $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">57,000</FONT> allowance against them.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Four of the nine commercial real estate loans, which amounted to $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3.0</FONT> million are classified as substandard in the Company&#8217;s allowance for loan losses and have a $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">220,000</FONT> allowance against them.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All such loans have been performing in accordance with their restructured terms and conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Company had one single-family nonperforming loan classified as a troubled debt restructuring in the amount of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">191,000</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The single-family loan was classified as substandard in the Company&#8217;s allowance for loan losses and had a $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">18,000</FONT> allowance against it.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All of the troubled debt restructurings consisted of changes in interest rates and no principal was forgiven.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013 and 2012, the Company had other borrowings of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3.4</FONT> million and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3.3</FONT> million, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Other borrowings consists of non-FDIC insured customer sweep investments.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The FHLB offers an alternative to regular repurchase agreements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The terms are variable from overnight to one year and utilizes mortgage loans as collateral in lieu of liquidity items such as government securities for collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company&#8217;s unused credit line with the FHLB amounted to approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">20.0</FONT></FONT> million at both December 31, 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition to the $20.0 million credit line with the FHLB, the Company had the ability to borrow an additional $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">152.7</FONT> million at December 31, 2013. </FONT></DIV>

<B>Income Taxes</B></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 11pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company uses the experience method in computing reserves for bad debts. <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The bad debt deduction allowable under this method is available to small banks with assets less than $500 million</FONT>. Generally, this method allows the Company to deduct an annual addition to the reserve for bad debts equal to the increase in the balance of the Company&#8217;s reserve for bad debts at the end of the year to an amount equal to the percentage of total loans at the end of the year, computed using the ratio of the previous six years&#8217; net chargeoffs divided by the sum of the previous six years&#8217; total outstanding loans at year end.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Retained earnings at both December 31, 2013 and 2012 included approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">7.1</FONT></FONT> million, representing bad debt deductions, for which no deferred income taxes have been provided.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has no liability recorded related to unrecognized tax positions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>No expense has been recorded or accrued for interest or penalties.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

</FONT>Loan originations are obtained by a variety of sources, including referrals from real estate brokers, builders, existing customers, advertising, walk-in customers and, to a significant extent, mortgage brokers who obtain credit reports, appraisals and other documentation involved with a loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In most cases, property valuations are performed by independent outside appraisers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Title and hazard insurance are generally required on all security property other than property securing a home equity loan, in which case the Company obtains a title opinion.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The majority of the Company's loans are secured by property located in its primary lending area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company had approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3.1</FONT> million and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">10.4</FONT> million in outstanding loan commitments, excluding unused lines of credit and the undisbursed portion of loans in process, at December 31, 2013 and 2012, respectively, which were expected to fund within the next three months.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank has an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (&#8220;ESOP&#8221;) for the benefit of employees who meet the eligibility requirements as defined in the ESOP.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The ESOP purchased <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">74,073</FONT> shares of common stock in the offering completed on January 30, 2007 using proceeds of a loan from the former mid-tier holding company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank makes quarterly payments of principal and interest over a term of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8</FONT> years at a rate of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8.25</FONT>% to the Company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The ESOP has a second loan from the Company to fund the purchase of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">150,991</FONT> additional shares in connection with the second step conversion completed on January 18, 2011 under which the Bank makes quarterly payments of principal and interest over a term of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">20</FONT> years at a rate of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3.25</FONT>% to the Company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The loans are secured by the shares of the stock purchased.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 4in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As the debt is repaid, shares are released from collateral and allocated to qualified employees.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As shares are released from collateral, the Company reports compensation expense equal to the current market price of the shares, and the shares become outstanding for earnings per share computations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The compensation expense for the ESOP for the years ended December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012 was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">189,000</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">161,000</FONT>, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 4in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

  <DIV

<B>Regulatory Capital Requirements</B></DIV>
</TD>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Failure to meet minimum capital requirements can initiate certain mandatory and possibly additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the Bank&#8217;s financial statements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, the Bank must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of the Bank&#8217;s assets, liabilities and certain off-balance-sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank&#8217;s capital amounts and classification are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings and other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Qualitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios (set forth in the following table) of Total and Tier 1 capital (as defined in the regulations) to risk weighted assets (as defined), and of Tier 1 capital (as defined) to average assets (as defined).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management believes, as of December 31, 2013, that the Bank meets all capital adequacy requirements to which it is subject.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013, the most recent notification from the FDIC categorized the Bank as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>To be categorized as well capitalized, the Bank must maintain minimum total risk-based, Tier 1 risk-based, and Tier 1 leverage ratios as set forth in the table.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There are no conditions or events since that notification that management believes have changed the Bank&#8217;s category.</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July of 2011, the shareholders of the Company approved the adoption of the 2011 Recognition and Retention Plan and Trust (the &#8220;2011 RRP&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Pursuant to the terms of the 2011 RRP, awards of up to <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">218,977</FONT> shares of restricted common stock may be granted to employees and directors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In order to fund the 2011 RRP, the 2011 RRP acquired <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">218,977</FONT> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock in the open market for approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2.4</FONT> million at an average price of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">11.14</FONT> per share.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>During 2012 and 2011, the Company made sufficient contributions to the 2011 RRP to fund the purchase of these shares.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Pursuant to the terms of the 2011 RRP, no additional shares will need to be acquired. On July 20, 2011, July 20, 2012, and December 11, 2013, a total of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">208,200</FONT>, <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3,000</FONT>, and <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">7,750</FONT> shares of 2011 RRP awards were granted, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The 2011 RRP shares generally vest at the rate of 20% per year over five years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Compensation expense on the 2011 RRP shares granted is recognized ratably over the five year vesting period in an amount which totals the market price of the common stock at the date of grant.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>During the year ended December 31, 2013, approximately <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">42,219</FONT> shares were amortized to expense, based on the proportional vesting of the awarded shares, resulting in recognition of approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">451,000</FONT> in compensation expense with a related tax benefit of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">153,000</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2013, approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.2</FONT> million in additional compensation expense is scheduled to be recognized over the remaining weighted average vesting period of 3.25 years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>During the year ended December 31, 2012, approximately <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">41,940</FONT> shares were amortized to expense, based on the proportional vesting of the awarded shares, resulting in recognition of approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">445,000</FONT> in compensation expense with a related tax benefit of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">151,000</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2012, approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.8</FONT></FONT> million in additional compensation expense was scheduled to be recognized over the remaining weighted average vesting period of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">4.5</FONT> years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the terms of the 2011 RRP, any unvested awards will become fully vested upon a change in control of the Company resulting in the full recognition of any unrecognized expense.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July 2011, the shareholders of the Company also approved the adoption of the 2011 Stock Option Plan (the &#8220;2011 Option Plan&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Pursuant to the 2011 Option Plan, options to acquire <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">325,842</FONT> shares of common stock may be granted to employees and directors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the 2011 Option Plan, options generally become vested and exercisable at the rate of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">20</FONT>% per year over five years and are generally exercisable for a period of ten years after the grant date.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>On July 20, 2011, July 20, 2012, and December 11, 2013 options to purchase <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">277,750</FONT>, <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">9,500</FONT>, and <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">38,500</FONT> shares of common stock were awarded, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2013, a total of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">92</FONT> shares of common stock have been reserved for future grant pursuant to the 2011 Option Plan.</FONT></DIV>

</FONT>The calculated fair value of options granted in 2011 was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2.99</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The fair value of each option grant is estimated using the Black-Scholes pricing model with the following weighted average assumptions for the options granted in 2012: dividend yield of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2.0</FONT>%, risk-free interest rate of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">0.71</FONT>%, expected life of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">7.0</FONT> years, and volatility of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">28.87</FONT>%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The calculated fair value of options granted in 2012 was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3.08</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The fair value of each option grant is estimated using the Black-Scholes pricing model with the following weighted average assumptions for the options granted in 2013: dividend yield of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2.0</FONT>%, risk-free interest rate of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.53</FONT>%, expected life of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">7.0</FONT> years, and volatility of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">28.35</FONT>%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The calculated fair value of options granted in 2013 was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">4.12</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The weighted average contractual term of the options outstanding was <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8.2</FONT> years and <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8.6</FONT> years at December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the years ended December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively, approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">167,000</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">162,000</FONT> was recognized in compensation expense for the 2011 Option Plan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively, approximately $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">568,000</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">583,000</FONT> in additional compensation expense for awarded options remained unrecognized. The weighted average period over which this expense will be recognized is approximately <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3.25</FONT> years and <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">4.5</FONT> years at December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively.</FONT></DIV>

<B>14.</B></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
<B>Fair Value Measurements and Fair Values of Financial Instruments </B></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management uses its best judgment in estimating the fair value of the Company financial instruments; however, there are inherent weaknesses in any estimation technique.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Therefore, for substantially all financial instruments, the fair value estimates herein are not necessarily indicative of the amounts the Company could have realized in a sales transaction on the dates indicated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The estimated fair value amounts have been measured as of their respective year-ends and have not been re-evaluated or updated for purposes of these financial statements subsequent to those respective dates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As such, the estimated fair values of these financial instruments subsequent to the respective reporting dates may be different than the amounts reported at each year-end. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FASB ASC Topic 820, Fair Value Measurement establishes a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to validation methods used to measure fair value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1 measurements) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level 3 measurements).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The three levels of fair value hierarchy under FASB ASC Topic 820 are as follows:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
&#160;</DIV>
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-COLLAPSE: collapse; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 10%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="10%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 1</FONT></I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 90%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="90%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: -6.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 6.5pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted assets or liabilities. <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 10%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="10%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></I></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 90%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="90%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: -6.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 6.5pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 10%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="10%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 2</FONT></I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: </FONT></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 90%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="90%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: -6.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 6.5pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Quoted prices in markets that are not active, or inputs that are observable either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the asset or liability.</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 10%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="10%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 90%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="90%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: -6.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 6.5pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 10%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="10%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 3</FONT></I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: </FONT></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #d4d0c8; BORDER-LEFT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 90%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #d4d0c8; BORDER-RIGHT: #d4d0c8; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="90%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: -6.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 6.5pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Prices or valuation techniques that require inputs that are both significant to fair value measurement and unobservable (i.e. support with little or no market value activity). </FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
<I></I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;</FONT>   <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>
  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="middle">
86</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 2px solid; FONT-STYLE: normal; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV>&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">An asset or liability&#8217;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following methods and assumptions were used to estimate the fair value of certain Company assets and liabilities:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash and Cash Equivalents (Carried at Cost),</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> The carrying amounts reported in the consolidated statements of financial condition for cash and short-term instruments approximate those assets&#8217; fair values. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Investment and Mortgage-Backed Securities,</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> The fair value of securities available for sale (carried at fair value) and held to maturity (carried at amortized cost) are determined by obtaining quoted market prices on nationally recognized securities exchanges for identical securities (Level&#160;1), or matrix pricing (Level 2), which is a mathematical technique used widely in the industry to value debt securities without relying exclusively on quoted market prices for the specific securities but rather by relying on the securities&#8217; relationship to other benchmark quoted prices.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans Receivable (Carried at Cost),</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> The fair values of loans are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses, using market rates at the balance sheet date that reflect the credit and interest rate-risk inherent in the loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Projected future cash flows are calculated based upon contractual maturity or call dates, projected repayments and prepayments of principal.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally, for variable rate loans that reprice frequently and with no significant change in credit risk, fair values are based on carrying values.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Impaired Loans (Generally Carried at Fair Value)</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">. Impaired loans are those in which the Bank has measured impairment generally based on the fair value of the loan&#8217;s collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Fair value is generally determined based upon independent third-party appraisals of the properties, or discounted cash flows based upon the expected proceeds.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Appraised values may be discounted based upon management&#8217;s historical knowledge and changes in the market conditions from the time of the appraisal.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Because of the high degree of judgment required in estimating the fair value of collateral underlying impaired loans and because of the relationship between fair value and general economic conditions we consider fair values of impaired loans to be highly sensitive to market conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These assets are included as Level 3 fair values, based upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The fair value of the impaired loans consists of the loan balances, net of any valuation allowance.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, the fair </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">value of the impaired loans consists of loan balances of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">5.3</FONT> million and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">12.0</FONT> million, respectively, net of valuation allowances of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">544,000</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.3</FONT> million, respectively; and loan balances of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">728,000</FONT> and $-<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">0</FONT>-, respectively, net of partial charge-offs of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">428,000</FONT> and $-<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">0</FONT>-, respectively.<FONT style="COLOR: black"> </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other Real Estate Owned.</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> OREO assets are originally recorded at fair value upon transfer of the loans to OREO.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Subsequently, OREO assets are carried at the lower of carrying value or fair value. The fair value of OREO is based on independent appraisals less selling costs.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Appraised values may be discounted based upon management&#8217;s historical knowledge and changes in the market conditions from the time of the appraisal.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Because of the high degree of judgment required in estimating the fair value of OREO and because of the relationship between fair value and general economic conditions the Company considers fair values of OREO to be highly sensitive to market conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These assets are included as Level 3 fair values, based upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, the fair value consists of OREO balances of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.1</FONT> million and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2.2</FONT> million, respectively, net of valuation allowances of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">155,000</FONT>, and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">313,000</FONT>, respectively.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FHLB Stock (Carried at Cost).</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> The carrying amount of FHLB stock approximates fair value, and considers the limited marketability of such securities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accrued Interest Receivable and Payable (Carried at Cost)</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">. The carrying amount of accrued interest receivable and accrued interest payable approximates its fair value.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deposits (Carried at Cost)</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">. The fair values disclosed for demand deposits (e.g., interest and noninterest checking, passbook savings and money market accounts) are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date (i.e., their carrying amounts).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Fair values for fixed-rate certificates of deposit are estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that applies interest rates currently being offered in the market on certificates to a schedule of aggregated expected monthly maturities on time deposits. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Borrowings (Carried at Cost)</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">. The carrying amount of overnight sweep accounts generally approximate fair value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>
  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="middle">
87</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 2px solid; FONT-STYLE: normal; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV>&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Off-Balance Sheet Financial Instruments,</FONT></B><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> Fair values for the Company&#8217;s off-balance sheet financial instruments (lending commitments and letters of credit) are based on fees currently charged in the market to enter into similar agreements, taking into account, the remaining terms of the agreements and the counterparties&#8217; credit standing. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following table summarizes assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of December 31, 2013, segregated by the level of the valuation inputs within the fair value hierarchy utilized to measure fair value (in thousands): </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><U><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Item 9A.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Controls and Procedures.</FONT></U></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'TmsRmn 10pt'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV align="justify">
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">a)</FONT></TD>
  <TD
style="WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
  <DIV align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the supervision and with the participation of the Company&#8217;s management, including its Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, the Company has evaluated the effectiveness of the design and operation of its disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act) as of December&#160;31, 2013. Based on such evaluation, the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that these controls and procedures are designed to ensure that the information required to be disclosed by the Company in reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and regulations and are operating in an effective manner.</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV align="justify">
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">b)</FONT></TD>
  <TD
style="WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Exchange Act Rule 13a-15(f). The Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (i)&#160;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the Company; (ii)&#160;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the Company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the Company; and (iii)&#160;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the Company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Internal control over financial reporting is designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements prepared for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the supervision and with the participation of management, including our principal executive officer and principal financial officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the 1992 framework in Internal Control&#151;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Based on our evaluation under the framework in Internal Control&#151;Integrated Framework, management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December&#160;31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">

&#160;</DIV>
</TD>
  <TD

  <DIV align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">c)</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
  <DIV align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">No change in the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act) occurred during the fourth fiscal quarter of fiscal 2013 that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</FONT></DIV>
